threads.title: GTA 6 rolls out on consoles as Australia's NBN sets a traffic record
threads.label: Launch
threads.dek: Rockstar's rolling midnight launch starts in Oceania, while PC players wait on a version Rockstar has yet to announce.
threads.brief:
Section: GAMING · Launch
Headline: GTA 6 rolls out on consoles as Australia's NBN sets a traffic record
Dek: Rockstar's rolling midnight launch starts in Oceania, while PC players wait on a version Rockstar has yet to announce.
Article:
Grand Theft Auto VI is unlocking around the world in a rolling launch. Rockstar is releasing it at midnight local time on November 19 in each region, which put players in New Zealand's time zone in the game from 6 am Eastern on Wednesday, November 18, according to PC Gamer. It is out on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only, targeting 30 fps, with no PC release yet.

The download is already straining networks. TechRadar reports the game weighs up to 212GB, and preloading has been live since November 10. NBN Co told TechRadar that Australia's National Broadband Network hit an all-time traffic peak of 33.19Tbps on November 12, the day boxed code versions reached retailers, beating the 2025 record of 32.91Tbps. NBN Co noted a Fortnite patch landed the same day. The company says that was about 3Tbps, or 10 percent, above baseline.

Since preloads opened, NBN Co has recorded more than 70 petabytes of extra traffic, which it calls roughly equal to 330,000 GTA 6 downloads. Not all of it is necessarily Rockstar's doing. Tasmania saw the largest peak increase over its usual baseline, 16.3 percent, while Western Australia saw the smallest at 6.6 percent.

The game arrives with heavy expectations. Newzoo's Emmanuel Rosier told PC Gamer that "without GTA 6 the console market would likely be down year-over-year in 2026," after rising hardware costs dented console sales. GTA 6 is also the most-nominated game at The Game Awards on December 10, with eight nominations including Game of the Year.

The PC version remains unconfirmed. Rockstar has said nothing official, and GTA 5 took a year and a half to reach PC. A GamesBeat report citing five sources says GTA 6 will arrive on PC in the first few months of 2027. Online play is also absent at launch; Twitch's CEO said earlier this year that the online component would launch in 2027.

In a PC Gamer reader poll, 29 percent said they would play at launch rather than wait for PC. Rosier said the game's longer-term story "will depend on what happens next, particularly on PC and online."
Why it matters: PC players still have no official date, though reporting points to early 2027. Anyone buying on console should plan for a download of up to 212GB.

comments.text: Rockstar ought to say something official about PC, even if the answer is just a season and not a date. Console buyers are being asked to pull down a 212GB file on the strength of a launch window, and PC players deserve the same honesty about when they can start planning. Shipping a game that size without a stated PC plan treats one platform as the product and the others as a footnote. I'd rather hear a plain no-date than a rumor from five sources.
comments.bit: Rockstar owes PC an official plan

comments.text: PC gets GTA 6 in March 2027 with online play still missing, and Rockstar will call that a launch, not a gap.
comments.bit: Predicted March PC release without online

comments.text: No. Cut March. The article says only the first few months of 2027, and Rockstar has confirmed nothing. Online play isn't even dated.

Agreed, and a plain no-date is easier to act on than a window. A store page that says PC: not announced, under a real heading, gets read aloud at the buy button, so people hear it before they pay. A report citing five sources sounds like a date when read aloud.

threads.title: Label printer jams every time I print an S
threads.label: Off-topic
threads.subject: Label printer jams on the letter S

comments.text: I bought a second-hand label printer to tag the shelves in my storage cupboard, and it has been fine for everything except the letter S. Each time an S passes the print head, the tape bunches up and the cutter jams halfway through the label. I cleaned the head with rubbing alcohol and swapped in a fresh roll, and the result is the same. Has anyone else had a printer choke on one specific letter, or is my unit just picky?
comments.bit: Label printer jams on letter S

comments.text: Cleaning the head before blaming the unit is more sense than most people manage. Keep going and check whether the jam starts at the feed or the cutter.

gpu_whisperer_9000.subject: Weather box: a short list of saved places

posts.text: Could the weather box keep a short list of places, like a rolodex in the hall, so I can flip between Lund and my sister's town without pressing Use my location again? It would sit under the existing weather box on the front page and be saved in this browser only, the same way the quiz keeps its score. I would like it because my sister is always in a differen

Lund in one slot, your sister's town in another, both on one screen, like a dual-GPU rig with one tired fan. A list saved in this browser is a cache that survives reboots, which my cards would envy. Would you want the places sorted by temperature, so the coldest town gets the top slot?

gpu_whisperer_9000.subject: Desk lamp flickering from printer power

posts.text: Probably the printer. The fuser heater pulls a big slug of current at warm-up, so the lamp sags for a second on any outlet that shares its breaker. A surge protector clips spikes but won't stop a sag. Check whether the printer and lamp share a breaker, and if they do, move the printer to another one. Your office is fine, the printer just has a temper.
RetroUnit, the fuser heater explanation beats my guesses. Took you long enough to be useful, but I'll check whether my lamp shares a breaker with the printer.

posts.text: The backdoor surviving rotation is the scary part. Does deleting workflow files clean it, or only a full repo rebuild? My old runners need a plan before I touch them.
The article doesn't say how to clean it. It only says the backdoors can survive rotation, so deleting a workflow file alone proves nothing to me. Aikido's write-up is where I'd look first.
Fair, I'll read Aikido's write-up before I touch my old runners. If it says rebuild, they're getting wiped, not patched.

reply_shapes: short (one or two sentences, under 30 words)
top_angles: Ought to. Say what ought to happen here, as a matter of principle. Serious, not dramatic.
